note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

precepts.why:
“Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus: every head was made bald, and every shoulder was peeled: yet had he no wages, nor his army, for Tyrus”. So God says, “Behold, I will give the land of Egypt unto Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall take her multitude, and take her spoil, and take her prey; and it shall be the wages for his army.”

He used what he took from Egypt as the pay. That is the wasting of Egypt in verse 11: when Nebuchadnezzar wiped out Egypt, “No foot of man shall pass through it, nor foot of beast shall pass through it, neither shall it be inhabited forty years.”

precepts.why:
A precept for the Egyptians: “Thus saith the Lord, The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature”. Men of stature means height, like the tall men of the Dinka tribe in the land of Pathros. “Shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall come after thee; in chains they shall come over, and they shall fall down unto thee, they shall make supplication unto thee, saying, Surely God is in thee; and there is none else, there is no God.”

That happened during the time of Persia and Media, when Cyrus came in power, and it’s going to happen again when Christ sits on the throne.

moments.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy
From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: In the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, the word came to set Ezekiel's face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers and says, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: The Most High will put hooks in his jaws, bring him up out of his rivers, and leave him thrown in the wilderness, because Egypt has been a staff of reed to the house of Israel that broke and tore their shoulder when they leaned upon it.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: The Most High will bring a sword upon Egypt, cut off man and beast, and make the land utterly waste and desolate from Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years, scattering the Egyptians among the nations.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: At the end of forty years He will bring the Egyptians again from where they were scattered into the land of Pathros, but they shall be a base kingdom, the basest of kingdoms, no more to rule over the nations or be the confidence of the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: In the twenty-seventh year the word came that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus, yet had no wages for it, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: Therefore the Most High gives the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his army, because they wrought for Him; in that day the horn of the house of Israel will bud forth and Ezekiel will be given the opening of the mouth in their midst.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: This occurred during the time of Nebuchadnezzar. When Nebuchadnezzar smote Egypt, the true Egyptians, the sons and daughters of Ham, were scattered, but after 40 years they came back to the land.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “And they shall be there a base kingdom.” Base is the root word of basement; you can get no lower, that’s the bottom. At one time ancient Egypt was the world’s superpower. The Lord said after Nebuchadnezzar smote them they would never rise again: “for I will diminish them, that they shall no more rule over the nations.” Kemet is just another word for Ham; when they say they’re Kemet, that’s Hamitic.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “And it shall be no more the confidence of the house of Israel”. When Nebuchadnezzar was going to come against us, our forefathers made a league with Egypt to help fight ancient Babylon, and that got wiped out; we got wiped out and Egypt got wiped out. The Lord had warned us through Jeremiah not to make a league with Egypt. Some of our people today believe Egypt is on the rise, but those ancient Egyptians you can’t even find today. Egypt was conquered by the Muslim Arabs in 641 A.D., the Ottoman Turks took over in 1517, and Turkish rule ended around 1952 when Gamal Abdel Nasser came to power. The modern Egyptians are Arabs, Ishmaelites, not Hamites at all.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: On the map you see Egypt, Sudan under that, South Sudan under that, and then Ethiopia. “I will make the land of Egypt utterly waste and desolate, from the tower of Syene even unto the border of Ethiopia.” Boyd’s Bible Dictionary says Syene was an important city during the reigns of the Shepherd kings in Egypt, now represented by the Arab village of Aswan. So Syene, when you’re reading the Bible, today they call it Aswan: you see the Aswan Dam right there in Egypt.

When you look at a modern map, Egypt is separated from the border of Ethiopia by Sudan. But the Bible never mentions Sudan at all. Why is that? It’s the same place. Egypt extended all the way down to the border of Ethiopia; upper and lower Egypt was one whole land mass, and Sudan was part of Egypt. The white man split it up.

Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt because it was the same place; Sudan and Egypt was one country. When people talk about pyramids they say I want to go to Egypt; nobody ever talks about Sudan, because nobody hardly knows there’s pyramids in Sudan. You got to thank the white man for that: hide everything but for themselves.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “Neither shall it be inhabited forty years”: write this down, Nebuchadnezzar. When Nebuchadnezzar wiped out Egypt, nobody lived there for 40 years.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations”: the Egyptians were scattered amongst Africa.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “And will cause them to return into the land of Pathros”: write this down, Pathros is Sudan, what they call Sudan today. “And they shall be there a base kingdom”: that’s where you got the Dinka tribe and all of them, especially in South Sudan; that’s where they’re at now. Look up the Dinka tribe: the shortest among them is like seven feet tall; the women are maybe six feet, but the dudes is like seven feet in height.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “It shall be the basest of the kingdoms”: Egypt, particularly the area of Sudan. Basest means the lowest of all the kingdoms. “Neither shall it exalt itself any more above the nations”: Egypt would never be exalted as a world superpower ever again. “For I will diminish them, that they shall no more rule over the nations.” You that are trying to glorify ancient Egypt: it will never rise again, thus saith the Lord. He made them the basest kingdom in the world today; you trying to resurrect them, you can’t resurrect them.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “And it shall be no more the confidence of the house of Israel”: back then we had confidence in Egypt. We made a league with the Egyptians and said, hey Dinka tribe, help us fight against Nebuchadnezzar. Jeremiah and them said don’t do that, you’re going to lose, God said just submit, and they got mad at Jeremiah. Nebuchadnezzar went through there and wiped Egypt out, and then got us in captivity.

Now today our people say ancient Egypt, we’re the Egyptians. We were not the Egyptians. We should have no confidence in Egypt: back then the confidence was wiped out. That’s what’s going on over there in Sudan right now; when God said I’ll make them the base kingdom, he meant that thing. “Which bringeth their iniquity to remembrance, when they shall look after them: but they shall know that I am the Lord God.”
